description.p: Verbinal is a native Linux companion for the CANFAR Science Portal: launch and manage science sessions, browse VOSpace, search the CADC archive, and look at the data without leaving the desktop.

ul.li: Launch, monitor, renew and delete sessions — Notebook, Desktop, CARTA, Contributed, Firefly and Headless — beside the VOSpace quota, the live cluster load and your recent launches.
Find a container image by what is installed in it rather than by its name, faceted by OS family and version.
Open and run Jupyter notebooks, with cell output rendered for every MIME type the parser models.
Keep research protocols as check-off step cards, from built-in templates or your own copies.

Search the CADC archive across four constraint columns, narrowed by a faceted data train — or write ADQL directly, checked against the service's own schema as you type, so a query that cannot work is refused before it is sent.
Save an observation whole — preview and FITS — into a local research library that then needs no network, with your notes attached, exportable as a single citable archive.

description.p: Its two viewers are built for astronomical data rather than for pictures:

ul.li: A FITS viewer with WCS, colormaps and stretches, percentile and zscale cut levels, an extension selector, a crosshair reading sky coordinates, and blink, linked-crosshair and synced-zoom comparison across tabs.
A cube viewer with GPU volume rendering and an opacity transfer function, plus a 2D slice view with a channel scrubber and per-voxel spectra.

description.p: Marks can be drawn on an image or a cube, labelled, moved and resized, each with its own colour, weight and thickness. They persist with the file and appear in exported figures, which carry the region's real sky coordinates, the cut levels and a colorbar.

An AI assistant can drive the whole application over a local MCP socket: read what is on screen, point at part of it, and hand back a figure. Writes are proposed and applied rather than silently performed.

A release about being told things when they happen. Notifications were a side effect of polling, so the interval was the delay; a session that had failed before the app started was announced on every launch. The images list now shows what you can actually launch, filtered by type and project, and images the platform does not publish can be searched for in the registry behind it and added to your own.

A release about being told the truth: an agent asking for something impossible was answered "done", the new ADQL checker had never once run, and the About window named the wrong versions. Underneath, three pieces of code that existed twice now exist once.

An imaging release. Marks can be drawn on a FITS image or a cube; an agent can see the working area and point at part of it; and sky coordinates on modern FITS headers, which were 40 to 90 arcseconds out, are fixed.
A notebook release: cell output is rendered for every MIME type the parser models, figures can be fetched as images, and two file formats that were destroyed by saving them no longer are.
